backup.about: A backup is one zip file in the library's backups folder: the database, the PDFs and the raw search answers, with a checksum for each. Copy it somewhere else (an external disk, a cloud folder) to keep it safe.
backup.restoreText: A backup is restored into a new, empty folder, which then opens as a library. Every file is checked against the backup's checksums. In this version, restore from a terminal:

external.intro: Databases without an open API (Scopus, Web of Science, TR Dizin…): save the query you run on their site, then import each export against it. Every import is its own search run; only records new since the last import enter screening.
external.saveFailed: The search could not be saved.
external.copied: Query copied. Paste it on the site.

guides.wos: Tick the records (or choose a range, up to 1,000 at a time) → Export → "RIS (other reference software)" → Record content: "Full Record" → Export. Plain text export comes when its preset is tested.
guides.scopus: Select all → Export → RIS → tick citation information and abstract → Export. CSV export comes when its preset is tested.
guides.jstor: Tick the results → Export citations → RIS.
guides.ebsco: Add the results to the folder → open the folder → Export → "Direct Export in RIS Format".
guides.proquest: Tick the results → "…" or Save → RIS → Continue.
guides.psycinfo: Export from the platform your library uses (EBSCO, ProQuest or Ovid) in RIS format.
guides.ieee: Select the results → Export → Citations → Format: RIS, Include: "Citation & Abstract" → Export.
guides.acm: Tick the results → Export citations → BibTeX → Download.
guides.scholar: Under each result, ❞ → BibTeX; paste the text into one .bib file, one record after another. Go slowly: Google shows a robot check if you click fast.
guides.trdizin: Open each publication's page and download it with the Ris button at the bottom. Choose RIS: the BibTeX file has no abstract.
guides.yoktez: The site exports no file, only formatted citations to the clipboard; add theses by hand.

search.thesesOnlyHint: Only OpenAlex and Crossref can be asked for theses; the other sources sit this search out.
